Boolean Multi-Hole Plate `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `Plate`: a rectangular slab of dimensions 4.0 x 2.0 x 0.2 BU centered on the world origin (so its z extent is [-0.1, +0.1]). Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. At the start of the task, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.

Produce `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` containing a single mesh object `Plate` carved with two features: - a 3x2 grid of cylindrical through-bores, axis along +Z, radius 0.15 BU, at x_i in {-1.2, 0.0, +1.2} and y_j in {-0.4, +0.4}; - a rectangular pocket cut into the top (+Z) face only, 2.0 x 0.8 x 0.08 BU, centered at (0, 0, +0.06), with pocket floor at z = +0.02. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists. 2. The scene contains exactly one mesh object named `Plate`, located at the world origin, with an empty modifier stack. 3. The mesh is closed-manifold — no non-manifold edges. 4. The mesh has no loose vertices and no loose edges. 5. The outer axis-aligned bounding box is unchanged: x in [-2, +2], y in [-1, +1], z in [-0.1, +0.1], each within tolerance 1e-3. 6. Each of the six bore centres is a true through-bore: a ray cast straight down at (x_i, y_j) from z = +1 finds no surface within z in [-0.2, +0.2]. 7. At six sample points on the top face that avoid both the pocket and the bores, a downward ray from z = +1 hits the plate top at z = +0.1 within tolerance 1e-3. 8. At the pocket centre (0, 0), a downward ray from z = +1 hits the pocket floor at z = +0.02 (within tolerance 1e-3), not the original top at z = +0.1. 9. Face count of the final `Plate` mesh is between 40 and 400 (inclusive). Clean up after cutting: no cutter objects may remain in the scene.
